questions.question_text: Find the sum of the roots of $2x^{3}+7x^{2}-5x+1=0$.

options.why: Forgot the negative sign in the sum formula $\alpha+\beta+\gamma=-b/a$.
Used the linear coefficient $c$ instead of the quadratic coefficient $b$.
Used the constant term $d$ instead of the quadratic coefficient $b$.
Inverted the sign of the pair sum $+c/a$.
Calculated the single sum $-b/a$ instead of the pair sum.
Calculated the triple product $-d/a$ instead of the pair sum.

questions.question_text: Find the product of the roots of $x^{3}-6x^{2}+11x-7=0$.

options.why: Forgot the negative sign in the product formula $\alpha\beta\gamma=-d/a$.
Evaluated the single sum $-b/a$ instead of the root product.
Evaluated the pairwise product sum $c/a$ instead of the product.

questions.question_text: If $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ are the roots of $2x^{3}-3x^{2}+5x-8=0$, find $\frac{1}{\alpha}+\frac{1}{\beta}+\frac{1}{\gamma}$.

options.why: Used an incorrect sign for the quotient $(c/a)/(-d/a)$.
Used $-b/a$ in the numerator instead of the pair sum $c/a$.
Inverted the numerator and denominator of the reciprocal sum formula.

questions.question_text:
Two roots of $x^{3}-7x^{2}+14x-8=0$ are $1$ and $2$.
What is the third root?

options.why: Applied an incorrect negative sign to the third root.
Subtracted $1+2=3$ from $-7$ instead of $7$ in the sum equation.
Took the product of roots without dividing by the product of known roots.

questions.question_text:
The roots of $x^{3}-9x^{2}+mx-24=0$ include $2$ and $3$.
What is the third root $\gamma$ and the coefficient $m$?

options.why: Used an incorrect sign for the pairwise product sum.
Used an incorrect negative sign when finding the third root.
Assumed a repeated root without checking the product of roots.

questions.question_text:
The cubic equation $x^{3}-4x^{2}-9x+k=0$ has two roots that sum to zero.
What is the value of $k$?

options.why: Used an incorrect sign in the constant term equation $-d/a=\alpha\beta\gamma$.
Divided by $2$ erroneously when combining root relations.
Used the wrong sign and divided by $2$ when evaluating $k$.

questions.question_text: For the cubic $4x^{3}-12x+7=0$, what is the sum of the products of the roots taken two at a time?

options.why: Omitted the negative sign on the linear coefficient $c=-12$.
Confused the linear coefficient $c$ with the missing $x^2$ coefficient $b=0$.
Calculated the product of all three roots $-d/a$ instead of the pair sum.
